summary: John's maternal 2nd great-grandmother; a foundling ('figlia di padre ignoto e madre ignota') born at Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi c.1873, wife of Frank Giannetta and mother of Mollie.
bio:
Not in the Ancestry tree; identified in Round 2. FS tree LCPG-FC6: born about 1874 in Bisaccia, immigrated 1909, died in Dunmore 1950. Mollie's 1931 license gives the mother as Angeli(c)a, maiden name 'Ferrandino', born in Italy; 'Angelina Genett' consented to the marriage. Frank's 1920 Declaration of Intention says his wife Angelina was born in Italy. Round 3 read the marriage act (Bisaccia, 1 Aug 1896, Matrimoni 1896 act 18): bride aged 23 (so born c.1873), born in Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi, resident in Bisaccia, 'figlia di padre ignoto e madre ignota' - i.e. a foundling; the surname Ferrantino was given to her by the authorities. Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi was a district seat with a foundling wheel (ruota); 'Ferrantino' is typical of names given to esposti. Her parents are unknown. The Sant'Angelo dei Lombardi registers on Antenati stop at 1865, so her foundling birth act (c.1873, probably via the ruota) cannot be reached there.

Angelica arrived in 1909, according to the 1920 census, with the children born in Italy; son Anthony's arrival is also recorded as 1909 ([R4-S2]). She had four children, all living, by April 1910, and three more were born in Dunmore ([R4-S1], [R4-S2]). After Frank's death in April 1934 she headed the household at 133 Sand Street, which she owned. In 1940 her sons Anthony and Charles J. lived with her, along with Charles's wife Jeanette and baby granddaughter Angela ([R4-S3]). Her daughter Mollie's family moved to 128 Sand Street nearby by 1950. The 1950 census, taken on 22 April 1950, shows her aged 75, widowed and naturalized, living with son Anthony and his wife Pearl at no. 133 ([R4-S4]). This gives a lower bound for her death, which FamilySearch places in 1950. Her ages run from 23 at her 1896 marriage and 46 in 1920 to 64 in 1940 and 75 in 1950, consistent with birth c.1873–1875.
